full_text:
Hyderabad: After days of scant rainfall,
Telangana is bracing for heavy to extremely heavy rain on Oct 28. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for three districts — Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem and Khammam — as a system over the Bay of Bengal is forecast to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and approach the Andhra Pradesh coast.
Nights in Hyderabad are also expected to turn cooler over the next few days, with the city’s minimum temperature forecast to fall to around 19°C on Oct 27 and 28.
The IMD’s seven-day forecast, issued on Sunday, said isolated places in the three red-alert districts could receive extremely heavy rainfall on Oct 28. An orange alert was issued for Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mahabubabad, Warangal, Hanumakonda and Suryapet, where heavy to very heavy rain was likely at isolated places.
The depression over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal was expected to intensify into a deep depression, then a cyclonic storm by Oct 26 and a severe cyclonic storm around Oct 27. It was forecast to strengthen further and cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of Oct 28 as a very severe cyclonic storm, with sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph and gusts of up to 140 kmph.
On Oct 28, rainfall is expected to spread across Telangana, with light to moderate rain or thundershowers likely at many places. Isolated places could continue to receive heavy rain on Oct 29.
Hyderabad, however, is expected to escape the worst of the weather. The city’s zone-wise forecast indicates light to moderate rain or thundershowers, accompanied by gusty winds of 30-40 kmph, on Oct 28 and 29. The expected impact across Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation zones is rated very low.
The forecast comes amid a sharp shortfall in rainfall. Telangana received 3.5 mm of rain against a normal of 75.6 mm between Oct 1 and 21, a deficit of 95%, according to IMD data.

full_text:
Andhra braces for ‘very severe’ Cyclone Arnab, IMD issues red alert
Deep depression intensifies into Cyclone Arnab, likely to turn very severe by Oct 27
The IMD on Monday said a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclone Arnab and is likely to strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm by October 27 before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast the following morning.
The cyclone lay centred over the eastcentral and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal at 5.30 am on Monday, moving westwards at 15 kmph during the preceding six hours, according to the IMD's National Bulletin No. 8.
"The deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclone Arnab and is likely to strengthen further into a very severe cyclonic storm by October 27 before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast on the morning of October 28," said the Met department in an official press release.
The system was located about 590 km northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram in the Andaman Islands, 650 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 730 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 830 km east of Machilipatnam and 910 km east of Bapatla, it said.
The weather system is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal by midnight on Monday, before strengthening further into a very severe cyclonic storm on October 27.
Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of October 28, with maximum sustained wind speeds of up to 125 kmph and gusts reaching 140 kmph, it said.
Under the influence of the system, thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are likely at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema. Heavy to very heavy rainfall, with extremely heavy rain at isolated places, is forecast over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on October 27 and 28. Heavy rainfall is also likely in parts of these regions on October 29.
Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) Managing Director Prakhar Jain said the next three days were extremely crucial and urged people to remain alert and strictly follow safety precautions.
Jain cautioned people against lowering their guard as the cyclone continued to develop over the Bay of Bengal.
He advised residents, particularly those in coastal areas, to comply with official advisories and take necessary precautions.

title: Looming cyclone raises hopes of rain relief for Telangana - The New Indian Express

full_text:
HYDERABAD: With Telangana recording an October rainfall deficit of 95%, a developing weather system over the Bay of Bengal has raised hopes of much-needed relief, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting heavy to very heavy rainfall across several districts on October 28.
The forecast comes amid concerns over declining water availability and the possible impact of El Nino on the state’s water resources.
The IMD has issued a red alert for Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem and Khammam districts, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall likely. Hyderabad, meanwhile, is likely to receive moderate rainfall.
The weather system is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on the evening of October 27, bringing rain to Telangana the following day, particularly in the eastern and northeastern parts of the state.
GNRS Srinivas Rao, senior meteorologist at the IMD Centre Hyderabad, told TNIE that the projected landfall location had shifted southwards. While the initial assessment suggested that the system would cross the coast between north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha, the latest assessment indicates a likely crossing between Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam.
“The system is expected to cross the coast on the evening of October 27, with its effects likely to be felt across Telangana on October 28, particularly in the eastern and northeastern parts of the state,” he said.
The IMD has issued an orange alert for Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mahbubabad, Warangal, Hanamkonda and Suryapet districts, forecasting heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on October 28. A yellow alert has been issued for Mancherial, Rajanna Sircilla, Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Jangaon, Nalgonda, Siddipet and Yadadri Bhuvanagiri districts, where heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places.
Srinivas said the system’s precise track and intensity would become clearer once it developed into a depression. As it was expected to move relatively quickly, its impact on Telangana was likely to be concentrated on October 28.
The IMD has also forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds at isolated places in Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Nalgonda, Suryapet, Mahbubabad, Warangal and Hanumakonda districts on October 28.
The possibility of rainfall is expected to extend into October 29. A yellow alert has been issued for Mancherial, Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Nalgonda, Suryapet, Mahbubabad, Warangal and Hanamkonda districts, where heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places.
With October rainfall already running at a deficit, the expected spell could offer some relief to the state. However, the extent of that relief will depend on the system’s eventual track and intensity, as well as the amount of rainfall it brings.
